children: Shares of Public Policy Holding were higher after the communications company said it has acquired New York-based communications firm Reevemark and entered into a new $105 million senior secured credit facility.
Shares of PPHC were up 7.3% to $11.09 as of midday Monday. The stock is down 1.7% this year.

PPHC said Monday that it has bought Reevemark for initial consideration of $28 million, with additional contingent consideration of up to $52 million. Reevemark is eligible for the maximum payout if it realizes roughly 35% compound annual profit growth through 2031.
The company expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to its earnings.

The acquisition will be funded in part by a new senior credit facility with a U.S. commercial bank, consisting of a $65 million term loan and a $40 million revolving credit facility. The new structure will also be used to refinance the company's debt and replace its existing credit arrangements.

The company plans to increase the size of the new facility to $150 million in total through commitments from additional lenders, with syndication expected to close in January. The new facility may also include an uncommitted accordion option of up to $50 million.

Reevemark, which will operate as a standalone business in the company's TrailRunner International group, adds expertise in litigation and crisis communications, PPHC Chief Executive Stewart Hall said.

The deal "positions PPHC as a global leader in litigation communications--one of the fastest-growing areas of our market--and adds market-leading expertise in transactions, shareholder activism, crisis and restructurings," he said.
